TOTAL PROFIT OVER LIFETIME

My Vehicle Profitability · TPOL

Understand what a vehicle earns, what it costs to operate and own, and the value it can deliver over its working life.

TPOL PILOT · ILLUSTRATIVE
How to use this first TPOL model: Start with one vehicle. Enter a representative month of revenue and operating costs, then add ownership and lifetime assumptions. The model separates operating performance from purchase/finance economics and clearly labels the result as an estimate until supported by verified records. Demo values below are examples only — they are not customer or UD performance data.

1. Vehicle investment & lifetime assumptions

Use the original purchase economics and expected working life. Do not enter monthly loan instalments here; finance interest is captured separately to avoid counting capital repayment twice.

2. Monthly revenue & operating costs

Enter the average monthly revenue attributable to this vehicle and its recurring operating costs. Operating costs exclude vehicle purchase price and finance interest.

Illustrative starter values loaded.

A transparent first estimate based on the inputs above.

KIZUNA Points proposal: TPOL onboarding and improvement milestones may qualify for points only after dealer/UD verification. Saving estimated figures does not automatically award points.
Important model limitations: This is a simplified planning estimate, not an accounting statement or financial advice. It assumes the entered monthly revenue and cost profile is representative across the vehicle's life. It does not yet model tax, inflation, discount rates, working-capital costs, downtime revenue loss, changing payload/route mix, major component replacements or year-by-year depreciation. A production TPOL model should support monthly history and verified data feeds.

My Fleet Benchmark

Understand your performance, compare it with relevant reference points and track verified improvement.

BENCHMARK PILOT
Important: There is no single universal heavy-truck benchmark. Results depend on vehicle specification, application, payload, route, terrain, traffic, fuel quality, maintenance and measurement method. Only the idling reference below is a published historical benchmark; the other targets must be agreed with your dealer using comparable fleet data. No customer or industry result is inferred from the demo.

1. Your performance baseline

Enter a consistent reporting period and use verified telematics, fuel, workshop and accounting records wherever possible.

CUSTOMER INPUT

2. Six performance indicators

Enter the customer's measured result. Add a comparison target only when it is supported by a source or agreed comparable UD/dealer cohort. Units and definitions must remain consistent.

Fuel efficiency

Higher is better. Compare like-for-like vehicle, route and payload.

Engine idling

Lower is better. 5% is a historical North American long-haul reference, not a universal norm.

Vehicle utilisation

Higher is not always better: consider demand, maintenance windows and fleet capacity.

Vehicle availability

Available time must use an agreed definition of planned and unplanned downtime.

Maintenance cost

Lower is generally better, but compare vehicle age, coverage and work scope.

Total operating cost

Define included cost categories consistently; connect this to TPOL.
No customer benchmark baseline saved.

3. Your improvement journey

KIZUNA Points proposal: 500 points for a dealer/UD-verified initial benchmark assessment; 250 points for a verified monthly update; and 500 points for a verified improvement milestone. Points are not awarded for entering estimates or merely saving this form. Production rules should include a defined baseline, minimum measurement period, comparable operating conditions and duplicate controls.
Reviewer simulation only.

4. Benchmark methodology & source register

The sources below support KPI definitions, data collection and selected historical reference points. They do not establish a universal set of current Southern African heavy-truck targets.

  • Logistics Cluster / World Food Programme — Fleet Performance Monitoring. Recommends monthly collection of distance, fuel, workshop days, fuel/maintenance/repair/tyre costs, availability, utilisation, cost/km and safety incidents. It explicitly says fuel consumption varies with road conditions, load, idling, air-conditioning, age and service condition. Its generic truck fuel baseline is not suitable as a direct customer target without matching duty cycle. Open source and methodology ↗
  • National Academies — Review of the 21st Century Truck Partnership, Chapter 4. Reports historical North American long-haul idling benchmarks as low as 5%, while warning that engine manufacturers calculate idle time differently. Treat 5% as a contextual reference only, not a pass/fail target for every KIZUNA customer. Open source ↗
  • Natural Resources Canada — Fuel Efficiency Benchmarking in Canada's Trucking Industry. Supports route-paired comparisons and collection of vehicle specification, average speed, idling and payload/GVW context. Its study is useful for comparison methodology, not direct African fuel economy targets. Open source ↗
  • South African Government Technical Advisory Centre — Comparative Spending Review of Fleet Management Practices. Describes cost-per-kilometre calculation and data-quality limitations from odometer capture. It concerns public-sector car fleets, so use it for calculation methodology only, not heavy-truck norms. Open report ↗
Future UD benchmark governance: Build anonymised peer groups from consented, verified UD customer data. Publish a cohort target only when there are enough comparable vehicles and periods; show sample size, country/region, vehicle/application segment, date range, data completeness and methodology. Never expose another customer's identifiable data.
